name: al-Qaeda (core network)
callout_language: Gulf and Levantine Arabic among foreign members; Pashto and Dari with local hosts; minimal radio, couriers and messengers.

doctrine.summary: The al-Qaeda 'core' (al-Qaeda central) is the leadership and shura of the global network founded by Osama bin Laden in 1988. After the deaths of bin Laden (2011) and Ayman al-Zawahiri (killed in Kabul by a US strike, July 2022) it has not publicly named an emir; UN monitoring reports and the US government assess Saif al-Adel as the de facto leader, based in Iran. The core today is a small, dispersed leadership with training facilities and safe houses in Afghanistan under Taliban tolerance (per UN monitoring reports), and it gives direction to stronger regional affiliates: AQAP (Yemen), al-Shabaab (Somalia), JNIM (Sahel) and AQIS (South Asia). In Syria, Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham broke with al-Qaeda in 2016-2017 and now forms the core of the Syrian government, and the al-Qaeda loyalist group Hurras al-Din announced its dissolution in January 2025, so al-Qaeda's Syrian presence in 2026 is limited to small remnant cells. In the game the core appears as small, well-hidden cells guarding couriers, safe houses and training sites, a classic HVT target set.
doctrine.fireteam: Cells of 3-6 around a courier, trainer or leader; local hosts provide guards. In game: 2-3 battle-buddy pairs.
tactics: Hide in remote compounds and mountain villages; guards fight a delaying action while the leader escapes
Courier movement by motorbike and civilian car, which the player must track
Small training sites in valleys guarded by a few fighters
Ambush from high ground on mountain tracks
Fall back into villages and among civilians, keeping the casualty rule active
IED-rigged compound entrances as telegraphed map hazards

notes: al-Qaeda is designated a terrorist organisation by the UN Security Council (1267 sanctions regime) and nearly every state. Affiliates in this pack: aqap (Yemen), al_shabaab (Somalia) and jnim (Sahel) are linked by pledges of allegiance (relations 85-90). Rivals: the Islamic State and its provinces (isis, isis_k) fight al-Qaeda affiliates where they overlap. Taliban: UN monitoring teams report continued al-Qaeda presence and ties in Afghanistan, which the Taliban deny; the positive relation to afg_taliban (an others-bloc faction) reflects that reporting and is low-confidence. Iran: the US and UN assess al-Qaeda leaders, including Saif al-Adel, live in Iran under restrictions; the relation is negative but less hostile than with IS. Syria: HTS (now the core of the Syrian government) split from al-Qaeda and Hurras al-Din dissolved in January 2025, so HTS is NOT part of this faction. Game framing: an early-game HVT and safe-house enemy, rather than a large field force. The value al_qaeda -> afg_taliban +40 is Captain-confirmed (2026-10-10).
